https://www.dw.com/en/ukraine-russia-pou.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IUD5 Without the necessary interceptors for its air defense, Ukraine is struggling to defend itself against relentless bombing by Russia Image: State Emergency Service of Ukraine/Handout/REUTERS Advertisement As Russia continues its relentless bombardment of Kyiv, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is making his first visit to Serbia , a European country that has maintained friendly relations with Russia despite the latter's full-scale invasion of Ukraine . Zelenskyy arrived in Belgrade Friday evening and had dinner with his Serbian counterpart, Aleksandar Vucic . They met again for talks at the presidential palace on Saturday. Later, Zelenskyy wrote on X that he and Vucic had discussed ways to strengthen infrastructure in both countries, including ports and railways, as well as economic development, reconstruction, and job creation in Ukraine and Serbia. Representatives from both countries signed a memorandum of understanding regarding agricultural and food safety cooperation. Zelenskyy added that the leaders also discussed the challenges of the upcoming winter in Ukraine, heavily hit by ⁠Russian attacks on energy facilities, and relations with the European Union. He also thanked Vucic for a new package of humanitarian support for Ukraine. Serbia supports Ukraine's territorial integrity Vucic said that Serbia will continue to support Ukraine's independence and territorial integrity, including the territories that Russia has seized since 2014. "You have never heard a single bad word about our country, not from Volodymyr Zelenskyy nor anyone else in Ukraine, and I am extremely grateful to our Ukrainian friends for that," Vucic said. The remark appeared to address the fact that Ukraine refuses to recognize Kosovo's independence, which was declared in 2008. Belgrade considers Kosovo to be part of Serbia. Vucic said he was skeptical that either Serbia or Ukraine would quickly join the European Union. However, he added that Belgrade would support Kyiv's bid. Serbia has repeatedly refused to put sanctions on Moscow. This has angered the EU and delayed Belgrade's path to joining the bloc. Both leaders also said their countries want to improve economic cooperation and finalize a free trade agreement by the end of the year. ​ D espite its dependence on Russian energy, Serbia has supplied nonmilitary aid to Ukraine. The Kremlin has accused Serbian firms of selling munitions to Ukraine, but Vucic has denied this claim. Vucic traveled to Ukraine for a regional summit in 2025 and again this year. Despite pledging aid to Ukraine, he has refrained from signing a formal declaration of support for Ukraine in the war. Russian attacks on Kyiv continue while Kyiv strikes Russian refineries The meeting came after at least four people, including a child, were killed in overnight Russian air attacks on Ukraine's capital, Kyiv, and the surrounding region, officials said on Saturday. "Last night, Russia killed three people in Pukhivka, Kyiv region, with drone strikes," Zelenskyy wrote on X. He added that the victims were a grandfather, a grandmother and their 3-year-old grandson. Authorities said three other members of the family and a neighbor who came to their aid were hospitalized. Ukraine faces Patriot missile shortage To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video At least one more person was killed in Kyiv in a strike involving six ballistic missiles against civilian infrastructure, according to Zelenskyy. Ukraine's air force reported downing or intercepting 135 of the 151 drones that Russia launched overnight. Meanwhile, Ukraine's General Staff announced that the military had attacked Russia's Ilsky and Syzran oil refineries overnight, resulting in fires at both locations. https://www.dw.com/en/kazakhstan-parliam.text: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5JGpK Kazakhs are voting in an election that was triggered by the adoption of a new constitution earlier this year Image: Pavel Mikheyev/REUTERS Advertisement Kazakhstan's 12.3 million eligible voters will elect the Central Asian country's parliament on Sunday. The polls come after a new constitution approved in March did away with the Senate to create a new unicameral Kurultai — a reference to the medieval councils of the region's nomadic past. Backers of the new body say it will give parliament more say in decision making, critics argue it will only cement the power of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev . The 73-year-old took the reins from authoritarian Nursultan Nazarbayev — who himself ruled the country for 30 years after the collapse of the Soviet Union — in 2019. The constitutional reform also opens the door for President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev to stay in power Image: Turar Kazangapov/REUTERS The pro-presidential Adilet party is expected to win an overwhelming majority in Sunday's vote, with a number of smaller parties loyal to Tokayev also pegged to enter parliament. Seven state-approved parties have been allowed to field candidates for the 145-seat parliament while genuine opposition parties have been banned. The election is taking place amid soaring inflation (which is hovering around 10.2%) and rising taxes, fueling concerns for the government — and particularly Tokayev — of a repeat of January 2022 cost of living unrest that left 238 protesters and police dead . Inequality, corruption led to Kazakhstan unrest To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video Press crackdown and financial strain color Kazakhstan's election Beyond financial strain, Sunday's vote is also taking place against the background of crackdowns on press freedom , with numerous reporters under house arrest and official criminal cases being brought against 10 independent journalists and bloggers. Tokayev, a former Soviet official and Kazakh diplomat who worked at the UN, has touted his reforms and justified the many changes he has initiated — including the introduction of the new constitution — as necessary in a fast-changing world. "Without a doubt, these elections will be remembered as perhaps the most interesting in our country's history," said Tokayev on Friday. "Amid unprecedented geopolitical tensions and mounting global challenges, we must firmly and consistently implement our strategy to transform Kazakhstan into a truly developed state," he added. Tokayev has sought to maintain a delicate balance between Moscow — with their shared Soviet ties — and the West since sanctions were imposed on Russia over its invasion of Ukraine . Resource-rich and strategically located Kazakhstan also has ties to China and the European Union . Although Tokayev has said that he has no plans of staying in power beyond his current term, the constitutional reform that 87% of voters backed this March effectively reset term limits for the office — making him eligible to run for another seven-year stint in 2029 should he change his mind. https://vietnamnews.vn/politics-laws/180.text: General Secretary, President Tô Lâm receives newly accredited ambassadors HÀ NỘI — General Secretary of the Communist Party of Việt Nam Central Committee and President Tô Lâm received in Hà Nội on Saturday the ambassadors of Palestine, the Czech Republic, Denmark, the Republic of Korea (RoK), Malaysia, Norway, the Netherlands, Belgium, Brazil, and France, who presented their credentials and officially began their terms of office in Việt Nam. Welcoming the ambassadors, the top leader highlighted their important role in effectively implementing agreements and commitments between Việt Nam and their respective countries, helping further deepen bilateral ties in a faster and more substantive manner for the mutual benefit of each country. He expressed his confidence that the ambassadors will successfully fulfil their missions and affirmed that Vietnamese ministries, sectors and localities stand ready to coordinate with and facilitate their work. Through the ambassadors, he conveyed his greetings and appreciation to the leaders of their respective countries for their attention to and efforts to promote relations with Việt Nam. He urged the diplomats to proactively propose specific projects, develop clear action plans and strengthen coordination with Vietnamese ministries, sectors and localities, with a view to delivering tangible benefits to the people, serving each country’s development goals and contributing to peace, stability, cooperation and prosperity in the region and the world. He briefed the ambassadors on Việt Nam's development orientations in the new period, stressing the need to fully leverage the strengths and potential of Việt Nam and countries, while meeting each side’s development needs. Việt Nam is advancing a new growth model, with science and technology, innovation and digital transformation serving as key drivers, towards achieving its development targets, including double-digit economic growth, he noted. The Party General Secretary and President said that Việt Nam recorded positive results in the first nine months of 2026, with economic growth approaching 10 per cent. In external relations, Việt Nam consistently pursues a foreign policy of independence, self-reliance, peace, friendship, cooperation and development, and diversification and multilateralisation of external relations. The country is also proactively promoting deep, substantive and effective international integration, creating a favourable environment for national development and contributing to peace, stability, cooperation and development in the region and the world. The ambassadors expressed their impression at Việt Nam's achievements and development, highlighting the country’s potential and prospects and expressing confidence that Việt Nam would achieve its development goals. They pledged to make every effort and work closely with Vietnamese authorities to further advance bilateral relations in a deeper and more substantive manner, while strengthening cooperation in such areas as economy, investment, science and technology, education and training, culture, and people-to-people exchanges, accompanying Việt Nam in its new era of development. Receiving Palestinian Ambassador Shadi Abu Zarqa, Party General Secretary and President Tô Lâm congratulated him on his appointment and conveyed greetings and an invitation to visit Việt Nam to President of the State of Palestine Mahmoud Abbas. Sharing the difficulties facing Palestine and its people, the host reaffirmed Việt Nam's consistent support for the Palestinian people’s legitimate struggle. He expressed his hope that during his tenure, the ambassador would contribute actively to strengthening the traditional friendship between Việt Nam and Palestine, particularly through people-to-people exchanges and cooperation in culture and education. Ambassador Shadi Abu Zarqa congratulated Việt Nam on its significant socio-economic achievements, expressing appreciation for Việt Nam's valuable support for the Palestinian people, which he said serves as a great source of encouragement for their cause. At his meeting with Czech Ambassador Lukas Kaucky, the General Secretary and President affirmed that Việt Nam attaches importance to its traditional friendship with the Czech Republic, one of Việt Nam's leading partners in Central and Eastern Europe and its first Strategic Partner in the region. He suggested both sides closely coordinating in implementing high-level agreements and deepening the new cooperation framework, while expanding trade and exploring new areas of collaboration, with the goal of raising bilateral trade to US$5 billion. He noted that the Czech Republic can serve as a gateway for Việt Nam to strengthen ties with Central and Eastern Europe, while Việt Nam is ready to act as a bridge for the Czech Republic to expand cooperation with ASEAN. He also expressed appreciation for the Czech Government’s support for the Vietnamese community in the country and called for continued coordination and mutual support at multilateral forums in the interests of regional and global peace, stability and prosperity. Ambassador Kaucky described his appointment as an honour, highlighting the long-standing bonds between the two countries. He underlined the important role of the Vietnamese community and generations of Vietnamese people who studied in the Czech Republic, as well as Czech citizens living and working in Việt Nam, as bridges between the two peoples. He affirmed that Việt Nam is among the Czech Republic’s key partners in the region and pledged to make every effort to further strengthen the Việt Nam–Czech Republic Strategic Partnership, while promoting comprehensive cooperation between Việt Nam, the Czech Republic and the European Union. Welcoming Danish Ambassador Lina Gandløse Hansen, General Secretary and President Lâm congratulated her on taking up her post as the two countries celebrate the 55th anniversary of diplomatic relations. He conveyed his greetings to the King and Queen of Denmark and expressed appreciation for Denmark’s valuable support for Việt Nam. He called for stronger political ties and greater economic, trade and investment cooperation, as well as effective implementation of the Green Strategic Partnership. He highlighted opportunities for expanded collaboration in energy, maritime and marine economic development, science and technology, innovation, green transition and digital transformation. Given Denmark’s strengths as a maritime power, he encouraged closer cooperation in the field and called for greater people-to-people exchanges, including the establishment of a direct air route between the two countries. Ambassador conveyed greetings from King Frederik X and reaffirmed Denmark’s commitment as a long-standing and trusted partner of Việt Nam. She said Denmark will continue supporting Việt Nam in implementing the Green Strategic Partnership and achieving its net-zero emissions target, while promoting cooperation in innovation, renewable energy, infrastructure and sustainable food systems. The ambassador pledged to contribute to making bilateral ties deeper, more substantive and effective. At his reception for Ambassador Lee Miyon of the Republic of Korea, the Vietnamese leader expressed his satisfaction with the positive and comprehensive cooperation achievemetns the two countries have attained since establishing diplomatic relations nearly 35 years ago. He called for continued delegation exchanges at all levels and effective implementation of bilateral commitments and agreements. He urged the two sides to strengthen practical cooperation in defence and security, create breakthroughs in economic ties, and effectively advance the new pillar of science and technology cooperation. He also called for efforts to reach the target of $100 billion in bilateral trade in 2026 and work towards $150 billion by 2030. He also asked the RoK to share experience and support Vietnam in successfully hosting APEC 2027, while promoting cooperation in culture, tourism, labour and local-level exchanges, and creating favourable conditions for the Vietnamese community in the RoK. The two sides should further coordinate and support each other on regional and international issues of shared concern, he said. Ambassador Lee expressed her honour at returning to Việt Nam as ambassador at a time when bilateral ties are developing strongly. She affirmed that the RoK attaches importance and gives priority to relations with Việt Nam, which she described as a key ASEAN partner across multiple fields. She expressed her hope that Korean businesses would have opportunities to participate in major projects in Việt Nam and pledged close coordination with Vietnamese authorities in preparations for the APEC Economic Leaders’ Week in Phú Quốc in 2027. The ambassador pledged to serve as a bridge of friendship and cooperation and contribute to making the Việt Nam–Republic of Korea Comprehensive Strategic Partnership increasingly substantive, effective and beneficial to both peoples. At his meeting with Malaysian Ambassador Jamal Sharifuddin Bin Johan, General Secretary and President Lâm congratulated him on his appointment and congratulated Malaysia on its successful ASEAN Chairmanship in 2025, which he said had made important contributions to regional cooperation, stability and development. He affirmed that Malaysia holds an important position in Việt Nam's foreign policy and expressed his wish to further deepen the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership between the two countries. The host noted positive developments across bilateral ties, particularly strong growth in trade and investment, active defence and security cooperation, and expanding collaboration in culture, tourism, education and people-to-people exchanges. He said substantial room remains for further cooperation. With both countries sharing the goal of becoming high-income developed economies, the Vietnamese leader suggested increasing the exchange of delegations at levels and finalising an Action Plan for 2026–30 soon to effectively implement the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. He also urged closer cooperation in the economy, defence and security, as well as greater collaboration in energy, maritime affairs, science and technology and innovation. The two sides should continue strengthening coordination, ASEAN solidarity and ASEAN centrality, while supporting each other at regional and international forums, particularly ASEAN and the United Nations. Ambassador Jamal Sharifuddin Bin Johan highlighted the elevation of bilateral ties to a Comprehensive Strategic Partnership during Party General Secretary Tô Lâm's visit to Malaysia in November 2024. Noting significant potential in trade, the halal industry and fisheries, the ambassador pledged to work closely with relevant agencies of both countries to strive for the $20 billion bilateral trade target and contribute to further deepening the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership. Welcoming Norwegian Ambassador Stein Iversen, the Vietnamese leader expressed satisfaction with the achievements in Việt Nam–Norway friendship and cooperation over the past 55 years and encouraged the ambassador to play an active bridging role in advancing bilateral relations. He welcomed the conclusion of negotiations on the Việt Nam–European Free Trade Association (EFTA) Free Trade Agreement, saying it would open up new opportunities for trade and investment. He for effective implementation of the Green Strategic Partnership, with a focus on maritime cooperation, while encouraging Norway to share its strengths and experience as a maritime power. He also highlighted potential for expanded cooperation in renewable energy, green transition, fisheries, climate change response, and science and technology. Việt Nam is ready to support Norway and serve as a bridge for stronger cooperation between Norway and ASEAN, he affirmed. Ambassador Iversen said Norway attaches importance to its friendship and cooperation with Việt Nam, describing the conclusion of the Việt Nam–EFTA FTA negotiations as an important milestone that, together with the Green Strategic Partnership, would provide fresh momentum for bilateral ties. He affirmed Norway’s readiness to continue supporting Việt Nam's green transition, plastic waste reduction and carbon emissions reduction, while encouraging Norwegian businesses to expand investment in Việt Nam. The ambassador praised Việt Nam's development achievements, its positions and contributions at the United Nations, support for multilateralism and role in ASEAN, and pledged to work to make Việt Nam–Norway relations deeper, more substantive and effective. Receiving Dutch Ambassador Remco van Wijngaarden, General Secretary and President Lâm highlighted the Netherlands’ position as one of Việt Nam's leading partners in Europe and spoke highly of the substantive results of the strategic partnership on climate change adaptation, water management, sustainable agriculture and food security. He called for stronger political trust through regular high-level exchanges and encouraged the study of a direct air route between Việt Nam and the Netherlands to enhance trade, tourism and people-to-people connectivity. He suggested the two countries work towards becoming models of cooperation in the maritime economy and sustainable development, while establishing new frameworks for collaboration in frontier areas such as science and technology, green energy transition, the circular economy, semiconductors and integrated circuits. He also emphasised collaboration in education and training, particularly high-quality human resources development. Ambassador Wijngaarden affirmed the Netherlands’ strong commitment to its reliable and effective partnership with Việt Nam, noting that the country is proud to be among the EU’s leading trade and investment partners of Việt Nam. He said he will prioritise coordinating high-level visits to create momentum for upgrading bilateral ties and focus on breakthrough cooperation in high technology, semiconductors, integrated circuits and smart, sustainable maritime economic development. At his meeting with Belgian Ambassador Pieter Leenknegt, Tô Lâm welcomed positive developments in bilateral relations, particularly following the successful state visit to Việt Nam by the King and Queen of Belgium in April 2025. Highlighting Belgium’s central role in the European Union, General Secretary and President Lâm described Belgium as an important partner and noted significant potential for expanded cooperation, particularly in energy, maritime transport and agriculture. He suggested both sides coordinate to create a strong shift in investment cooperation, promote the role of Việt Nam and Belgium as gateways linking ASEAN and the EU, and elevate science, technology and innovation as priority areas of bilateral collaboration. Ambassador Leenknegt spoke highly of Việt Nam's strategic development achievements, particularly its progress in wind energy. He affirmed Belgium’s readiness to support Việt Nam in energy cooperation and the implementation of its Just Energy Transition Partnership (JETP) goals. Noting the active presence of Belgian investors in Việt Nam's energy and port sectors, the ambassador said the two countries still have substantial room for cooperation. He pledged to contribute to stronger multifaceted ties and promote exchanges between Vietnamese localities and Belgian regions. Receiving Brazilian Ambassador Marcelo Paz Saraiva Camara, the Vietnamese leader affirmed Việt Nam's desire to further strengthen its Strategic Partnership with Brazil, one of Việt Nam's key partners in Latin America. He welcomed positive developments in bilateral ties, including regular high-level exchanges, the elevation of relations to a strategic partnership in 2024, continued growth in economic and trade ties, and expanding cooperation in science and technology, innovation, digital transformation, green devel

The prospective trip follows a telephone call between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin in which the Russian leader spurned peace talks and vowed to press ahead with the war, as well as inconclusive multilateral consultations in Miami and controversy over a US-Russian diesel agreement. by Kyiv Post | Oct. 11, 2026, 9:04 am Flip Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law Jared Kushner (L) and US Special Envoy Steve Witkoff (R) attend a meeting with Russian president in Moscow on September 5, 2026. (Photo by Gavriil GRIGOROV / POOL / AFP / Sputnik) Content Share Facebook X (Twitter) LinkedIn Bluesky Email Copy Copied Flip US special envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner may visit Russia in the coming weeks following a phone conversation between US President Donald Trump and Russian President Vladimir Putin , Russian state news agency TASS reported. Citing Russian sources, TASS reported that the trip could take place within the next two weeks, although specific dates have not yet been finalized. JOIN US ON TELEGRAM Follow our coverage of the war on the @Kyivpost_official . A source confirmed the likelihood of another visit by the US representatives, noting that technical details and schedules remain subject to bilateral coordination. The reports of prospective travel follow a telephone conversation on Friday, Oct. 9, between Trump and Putin. Following that call, Kremlin foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov told Russian state media that Putin reiterated Moscow’s intent to sustain military operations until all Kremlin objectives are fulfilled, rejecting the resumption of formal peace negotiations. Advertisement Ushakov claimed that Trump instructed American officials to relay the diplomatic positions articulated by Moscow directly to the Ukrainian government. Diplomatic outreach following Miami consultations The prospective trip follows multilateral consultations convened by the US in Miami on Friday , Oct. 9. The six-hour session brought together Witkoff, Ukrainian negotiators, and representatives from Britain, France, Germany, the European Commission, and NATO to discuss prospective security arrangements and measures to protect Ukrainian energy infrastructure ahead of winter. Other Topics of Interest ‘I Love the Smell of Russian Gas’: Controversial Polish Politician Backs Nord Stream Grzegorz Braun urged Poland to help revive Nord Stream during an appearance with Germany’s far-right AfD, drawing accusations of “shame and treason.” While Witkoff described the discussions on social media as “constructive” and aimed at exploring avenues to conclude the armed conflict, the talks concluded without an announced breakthrough. European and Ukrainian officials have expressed skepticism regarding Moscow’s willingness to engage in substantive de-escalation. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha warned on Friday that offering economic or diplomatic concessions to Moscow projects weakness , arguing that the Russian leadership interprets accommodations as appeasement rather than incentives for peace. Advertisement Witkoff and Kushner previously traveled to Moscow and Kyiv in September to meet with senior government officials, as the Trump administration formulated proposals to address the diplomatic impasse. The prospect of renewed direct contacts in Moscow coincides with debate surrounding Trump’s announcement of a bilateral commercial agreement permitting Russian petroleum shipments into American and global markets. Under the arrangement announced by Trump on Friday, Russia agreed to supply 300,000 metric tons of diesel fuel immediately, with 500,000 tons scheduled for November and 1 million tons thereafter, potentially scaling up to 3 million tons depending on the operational condition of Russian refineries. The US Treasury Department subsequently issued a temporary general license authorizing transactions involving Russian diesel through April 7, 2027. The sanctions waiver was granted three weeks after Trump signed into law the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 , which aimed to expand statutory penalties across Russia’s energy, banking, and defense sectors. Ukrainian officials, including President Volodymyr Zelensky, criticized the timing of the commercial arrangement while peace delegations were actively negotiating in Miami, cautioning that permitting Russian fuel exports generates revenues that sustain Moscow’s wartime budget.
